item.title: Envlope 1.8
item.description:
Variable sets per team, and env files that show where values come from.

New

  • Variable sets by team. Settings lists sets by owner: your own (synced to your Macs only), then one group per team (everyone on the team gets them). Create a set right in the group it belongs to; the picker next to a set moves it.
  • Env files show their sets. When you Apply a profile that uses variable sets, each set's variables are written under a # From set "Sentry" comment, then the profile's own under # From "Local". If a set and the profile both have a key, the profile's value is written, under the profile.

Changed

  • The command line tool and MCP server are no longer included while they're being tested. If you installed them from 1.6 or 1.7, remove the links with sudo rm /usr/local/bin/envlope /usr/local/bin/envlope-mcp.

Install

Envlope 1.6 and later offer this update by themselves (or use Envlope → Check for Updates…). Otherwise download Envlope-1.8.dmg below and drag Envlope to Applications; your data stays. Requires macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel). Signed by Creative Oak ApS and notarized by Apple.

item.title: Envlope 1.7.1
item.description:
Fixes the window going blank in 1.7.

Fixed

  • Projects with a status card made the window go blank. When a project showed a card (missing keys, or an env file that differs from the profile), the card's text could be measured far too tall, pushing the project view and the sidebar out of the window. Cards now wrap their text normally.

Install

Envlope 1.6 and 1.7 offer this update by themselves (or use Envlope → Check for Updates…). Otherwise download Envlope-1.7.1.dmg below and drag Envlope to Applications; your data stays. Requires macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel). Signed by Creative Oak ApS and notarized by Apple.

item.title: Envlope 1.7
item.description:
History, nicknames, and clearer project status.

Everyone sharing projects should update. Projects saved by 1.7 carry history, which 1.6 would drop, so 1.6 leaves them alone and shows "Update Envlope" until it updates.

New

  • History. The History button next to a project's folder lists every change to its profiles: who made it, when, and the value before and after (secret values stay masked until revealed). Restore puts an old value back. History syncs with the project, so everyone who has it sees the same list.
  • Nicknames. Set yours in Settings → You. People you share with see it in their member lists and next to your changes in History.
  • Link several projects at once. Select several folders, drop a folder of projects (like ~/Developer), or use File → Link Projects in Folder…. Tick the ones you want and choose Personal or a team.
  • Add a project straight to a team with the + next to the team in the sidebar, or the "Add to" choice when linking.
  • Linking is explained first. Before a folder is linked, Envlope shows which files become profiles and which list the keys a profile should have. The files stay where they are.
  • Open the env file in your editor with the button next to the folder path. Choose the editor in Settings → Env files.

Clearer status

  • Missing keys are checked against the matching example file (.env.local.example for Local, .env.example otherwise), and the warning says which file lists them. Add as Empty adds them for you to fill in.
  • When the env file doesn't match the profile, a card says how many keys differ and how. Compare lists them grouped as different values, only in the file and only in Envlope, with Apply and Capture right there.
  • Capture now shows the changes and asks first, like Apply, since the profile syncs to everyone who has the project.

Install

Envlope 1.6 offers this update by itself (or use Envlope → Check for Updates…). Otherwise download Envlope-1.7.dmg below and drag Envlope to Applications; your data stays. Requires macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel). Signed by Creative Oak ApS and notarized by Apple.

item.title: Envlope 1.6
item.description:
Envlope now updates itself, can back up everything to an encrypted file, and fixes a security problem in team projects shared outside their team. Everyone should update; on 1.5 or older, download this version by hand. From now on Envlope updates itself.

Security

  • Fixed: a teammate could make your Mac join a share they control (introduced in 1.5). Through it, new personal variable sets could end up where they could read them. Envlope now only joins a project's share when it is exactly the project it claims to be and its owner is on the team, and never reads or writes a zone that merely has the same name as one of yours.
  • People a project is shared with can change its contents, but not which team gets access to it.
  • A team project whose owner leaves the team stops syncing for the team. If you're removed from a team, projects you had changed keep your edits as personal copies.

New

  • Automatic updates. Envlope checks once a day and asks before installing. Updates are signed by Creative Oak and checked before anything is unpacked. See Settings → Updates.
  • Backups. File → Export Backup… saves every project, profile, value and variable set into one file, encrypted with a password you choose. Import Backup… adds what isn't on the Mac.
  • Command line tools inside the app. envlope and envlope-mcp now ship in Envlope.app and update with it. Install them from Settings → Command line and agents, which also copies the MCP config for your agent. If you copied the tools from an earlier DMG, install again and point your agent's MCP config to the new path.
  • Welcome screen, a notice when iCloud isn't signed in, and Help menu links to the guide and privacy policy.
  • Newer versions are respected. If another Mac saves data with a newer Envlope, this version leaves it alone and asks you to update, instead of overwriting it.

Install

Download Envlope-1.6.dmg below, open it and drag Envlope to Applications, over the old version; your data stays. Requires macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel). Signed by Creative Oak ApS and notarized by Apple.
